• LA Life •

Scholarship Prep South Bay in Wilmington kept every one of its homeless students from being chronically absent last year by building free meals, transit passes, laundry access and calming spaces right into the school day. The approach helped the school post the lowest chronic absenteeism rate among LAUSD's 787 schools, and LAUSD just renewed its charter for another five years. It is a hopeful example of what support-first schooling can look like. (Via Invisible People)

08 · 2027 Resolutions

Sponsored by Scan Squirrel

• LA Life •

Ashleigh Ellis built Unity Ice Academy to give Los Angeles kids free and low-cost access to figure skating, growing from one summer camp into a year-round program serving more than 150 kids with tutoring, meals and mentorship built in. Team USA figure skater Starr Andrews now coaches alongside Ellis, giving young skaters a rare chance to see someone who looks like them excelling in the sport. It is an inspiring model of what access and representation can do for LA kids. (Via neongurl)

• LA Life •

Pasadena high schooler Apollo Wong founded Glean On Me to send student volunteers into neighbors' yards across the San Gabriel Valley to pick unused fruit before it rots, then deliver it to local charities. The project has grown to more than 250 volunteers and 11,000 pounds of rescued produce, reaching food banks like Union Station and Friends In Deed. Wong was recently honored as a 2026 Daily Point of Light for the effort. (Via The Times of India)​
